issues.subject: Pound Sense: October rates, a warm flat and the bill in between
issues.text:
Pound Sense · {date}

October rates, a warm flat and the bill in between

We've updated the rate table for 21 October. Two easy-access accounts slipped down the list and the cheapest electricity quote in our sample changed with the postcode.

The easy-access table
Mere Building Society is advertising 3.82% AER on its online saver, with the rate on balances up to £20,000. Kipwick's 3.95% headline includes a bonus that runs for six months from opening. On our sheet you can see the underlying rate beside the headline. If you're moving a deposit you might need next month, check the daily withdrawal limit in the account details before transferring the lot.
https://poundsense.example/savings/october-table-21

Read the standing charge as well
We ran the same annual usage figures for a one-bed flat in E5 and a studio in SE15. The estimates were £68 apart even with the same supplier and payment method. With low usage, a few pence a day on the standing charge made more difference than we'd expected. The worksheet has a row for both charges and a box for the end date of your current deal.
https://poundsense.example/energy/october-flat-comparison

A photo before the heating goes on
If the meter cupboard is shared, get the serial number and the reading in one picture. A reader on the fourth floor of a converted house found he'd been copying the number from the flat above. The managing agent helped him label both meters once he sent the pictures. We've put the four questions he sent the agent in the note, along with a blank log for readings.
https://poundsense.example/renting/first-meter-reading

Back next Wednesday,
Ruth Fenner, editor

issues.subject: Pound Sense: Moving a cash ISA and trying a smaller flat
issues.text:
Pound Sense · {date}

Moving a cash ISA and trying a smaller flat

Three readers asked the same question about ISA transfers. We tried two providers' forms and took a tape measure to a rental viewing.

The transfer box you'll need
At Dewstead Savings the account reference on the statement includes a space that the transfer form strips out. At Mere Building Society the form asks whether you want to move everything or leave part of the balance behind. Make a note of whether your existing account has a notice period. We've put the relevant boxes side by side in the screenshots, with the sample account numbers covered.
https://poundsense.example/savings/cash-isa-transfer-forms

When a viewing lasts ten minutes
A reader nearly traded a high rent for a cheaper place with no room for her desk. We put ceiling height, radiator position and the width of the door on one side of a sheet you can carry round. Check whether the cheapest broadband quote is actually for the flat number. At the place we visited, the postcode checker showed fibre and the individual address showed a different service.
https://poundsense.example/renting/smaller-flat-viewing

The cash drawer experiment
One of our testers set aside £35 for seven days of small purchases. She made it to Friday with £12, then spent most of that on food at the station. Her note about keeping a lunch in the office freezer got more replies than the spreadsheet. The revised sheet has a space for things you can do earlier in the day, when you still have a choice.
https://poundsense.example/budgeting/cash-drawer-week

Back next Wednesday,
Ruth Fenner, editor

issues.subject: Pound Sense: A renewal offer with two prices
issues.text:
Pound Sense · {date}

A renewal offer with two prices

The rent number at the top of a renewal email is easy to spot. We looked at where recurring costs appear in the paperwork and when a savings bonus drops away.

What comes with the new term
Our sample renewal offered twelve months at £1,420 and a shorter term at £1,460. The PDF also put the shared heating contribution under a new heading eight pages down. We copied both options into a simple table with columns for what is paid monthly and what changes once in the year. If you've got an old agreement to hand, pull its figures straight from the signed copy.
https://poundsense.example/renting/renewal-cost-columns

Winter electricity payment check
Cress Electric's example statement shows a smaller summer balance on the first page and a higher suggested payment inside. We asked the company where it had got the annual usage estimate. Its reply was based on the last twelve bills, including three estimates. Our worksheet shows where you can enter meter readings alongside the bills, so a correction can be made with the right dates to hand.
https://poundsense.example/energy/direct-debit-worksheet

What the bonus is worth in pounds
Norwold's sample account gives its higher rate for four months. We put £4,000 into the calculator and showed the interest during the bonus separately from the eight months afterwards. The cash difference was smaller than the headline made it look. If an account has a minimum balance or a limit on how often you can withdraw, put that next to the pounds figure while you are comparing.
https://poundsense.example/savings/bonus-rate-calculator

Back next Wednesday,
Ruth Fenner, editor

issues.subject: Pound Sense: The moving-out folder
issues.text:
Pound Sense · {date}

The moving-out folder

This week's folder fits on a phone. Set it up before the keys go back, while the meter and the big scuff behind the wardrobe are still easy to photograph.

Make a set of matching pictures
A Willesden reader sent us two inventories taken from opposite ends of a room. It took some squinting to work out whether they showed the same mark. Start at the door and photograph each wall in order, then take close-ups with something for scale. Save the pictures alongside the agent's original inventory and note the date the last keys were handed over. Our example takes seven pictures.
https://poundsense.example/renting/matching-inventory-pictures

The first bill at the new place
The meter serial on a sample bill from Cress Electric was tucked into the usage panel. We circled it and the dates the charge covers. A reader who moved into a split house found the supplier had the wrong entrance on record. She used a picture of the meter and its serial number to show which supply belonged to her flat. Keep both when you first read it.
https://poundsense.example/energy/new-address-first-bill

Keep the moving money reachable
A Friday move can involve the van, two sets of keys and a card payment to replace a broken kettle. Check where the money for those last bills is sitting. Norwold's notice saver displays an estimated release date before you confirm a withdrawal. We put a sample month's moving costs on one page, with the deposit listed separately so it doesn't get counted twice.
https://poundsense.example/savings/moving-week-cash

Back next Wednesday,
Ruth Fenner, editor

issues.subject: Pound Sense: Small balances and long waits
issues.text:
Pound Sense · {date}

Small balances and long waits

The question in the postbag this week was whether moving a small savings pot was worth the paperwork. We put actual amounts in the columns and added a check for anyone sorting bills with a new housemate.

Three rates on £600
The difference between 3.3% and 3.9% on £600 works out to about £3.60 for a full year if the rates and balance stay put. We also showed the difference when you're adding £40 a month. Both figures are on the sheet. The third line is for your current account, because knowing what you have is the quickest way to rule some of the offers out.
https://poundsense.example/savings/six-hundred-pounds-compare

One bill, two surnames
After a housemate moved, one reader kept getting email addressed to the person who had left. The current account holder sent the supplier a photo of the closing reading and both dates, the day the old housemate left and the day the new one took the keys. The supplier then sent a revised statement. The note lists what our reader needed when she talked to its billing team.
https://poundsense.example/energy/shared-bills-note

Ten minutes for an ISA check
Pull up the rate and condition pages for any cash ISA you already opened. Some providers put maturity instructions in your messages rather than next to the balance. Our example view from Dewstead shows how to download an old statement and where we found the end date. Write down the provider's account reference while you're there. It saves you opening three statements when you next compare a transfer.
https://poundsense.example/savings/isa-autumn-check

Back next Wednesday,
Ruth Fenner, editor

issues.subject: Pound Sense: What a fixed bill actually fixes
issues.text:
Pound Sense · {date}

What a fixed bill actually fixes

Two readers sent us near-identical quotes with quite different monthly payments. We checked the small print and added a modest pay-day experiment for the reader who has plenty of standing orders already.

Same tariff, different estimate
Our pair of Cress quotes used the same unit rates. One was built from a flat with electric hot water and one was built from a default two-bedroom estimate. When we copied in the actual annual usage from the last bill, the quotes came closer together. The calculator now accepts separate day and night figures, and the example shows why combining those readings too early can distort the total.
https://poundsense.example/energy/two-quotes-one-tariff

Track the payment, not the pot
A reader trying to save for new curtains set her transfer to go out the day after payday. The money arrived on a Monday, the bills came out on the Tuesday and the standing order left too little for the weekly shop. She moved the savings date to the following Friday. We drew her before-and-after calendar so you can see which change freed up the money.
https://poundsense.example/budgeting/payday-standing-order

Files for the next rental viewing
A letting agent's portal in our sample accepted separate PDFs for payslips, while another asked for one combined document. Keep the working copies and make one export at a time. The folder list includes a place to write the name of the person who asked for the document and what they said they needed it for. There is also space for the amount and date of an advertised holding payment.
https://poundsense.example/renting/rental-viewing-files

Back next Wednesday,
Ruth Fenner, editor
